name: Question 11
worked_solution:
We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(0.1<Z<1.5).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069404/assets/806631e940119accaf9fa2dd9e52e59f4ae16480f237c2bb67ddc7796e4967c0.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.1<Z<1.5) & =P(Z<1.5)-P(Z\le 0.1) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.5)-P(Z\le 0.1) \\  & =Φ(1.5)-Φ(0.1).\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.1) & =0.5398 \\ Φ(1.5) & =0.9332\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.1<Z<1.5) & =Φ(1.5)-Φ(0.1) \\  & =0.9332-0.5398 \\  & =0.3934.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We're given that Z∼N(0,1), and we wish to compute P(0.1<Z<1.5). The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function Φ(z),

P(Z≤z)=Φ(z).

So, we express the required probability in terms of Φ(z):

P(0.1<Z<1.5)=P(Z<1.5)−P(Z≤0.1)=P(Z≤1.5)−P(Z≤0.1)=Φ(1.5)−Φ(0.1).

From the tables, we have the following:

Φ(0.1)=0.5398Φ(1.5)=0.9332

Therefore, we have

P(0.1<Z<1.5)=Φ(1.5)−Φ(0.1)=0.9332−0.5398=0.3934.
